greece.call: Buy speed only where it buys daylight

greece.q: Santorini and Mykonos, or the islands that cost less and crowd less?
Where does Crete fit, and why not in an island-hopping week?
greece.call: Crete is a trip, not a stop

greece.q: Where does the money actually leak on a Greek island week?
Ferry or domestic flight, and the island-to-island trap?
greece.call: Fly the long legs, ferry the hops

greece.q: How long in Athens, and is it worth the days?
greece.call: Give Athens two or three days

greece.q: The Oia sunset — how not to waste the one you came for?
greece.call: Have a sunset plan, not a sunset hope

morocco.call: For a first trip, seven days on the Marrakech–desert–Fez line is the sweet spot our reporting keeps returning to, and the open-jaw ticket is what makes it work
If you have three days, go to Merzouga; the extra night is the entire point
Use the train as the dependable spine wherever it runs

morocco.q: Who's paying the person showing you around?
morocco.call: The tell is a single question: who pays this person? If it's you, their incentive aligns with yours

morocco.q: How do you eat well without eating like a tourist?
morocco.call: Learn four dishes and you can read any menu in the country

thailand.q: What may you actually drive, and what are you insured on?
thailand.call: Count the endorsement before you count the fare.

thailand.q: How many islands actually fit, and in what order?
Which island — and which side of the line?
thailand.call: The island is not chosen from a photograph; it is chosen from the left-hand columns.

thailand.q: How do the legs connect, and who owns the failure?
thailand.call: The question is never which leg is fastest. It is which leg, if it fails, you have to buy twice.

thailand.q: What are you exposed to, and what does a policy actually answer?
thailand.call: Two questions to the insurer, before buying: do you direct-bill in Thailand, and does this policy include repatriation as well as evacuation?

thailand.q: Bangkok: where do you sleep, and how do you cross it?
thailand.call: If you want the lowest-friction first choice, book near Asok and stop deciding.

thailand.q: The temple door, and the elephant question
thailand.call: Apply the riding test first. If a venue passes it, read the table above for the rest.

thailand.q: Ordering well, without a reservation system you can use
thailand.call: Follow the crowd, start at mai phet, and work up.

japan.q: What does a day trip cost you?
japan.call: Under a week, take none. At ten days, take two.

japan.q: Does the national rail pass pay for itself?
japan.call: Count your long journeys before you buy, not after.

japan.q: Which card will load on an American phone?
japan.call: Create the card at home, load it with the card you intend to use, and watch the top-up complete before you fly.

japan.q: When should you come, and what does the date cost?
japan.call: If the dates are yours to choose, take late November.

japan.q: Which station should you sleep next to?
japan.call: Sleep on the Yamanote loop, and in Kyoto ignore the subway entirely.

japan.q: Is the ryokan worth it, and where should it be?
japan.call: One night, in an onsen town, not in Kyoto.

japan.q: How do you eat well without a reservation system you can use?
japan.call: Book two meals for the whole trip and let the rest happen.

japan.q: Which airport, and what happens in the first six hours?
japan.call: Pay a modest premium for Haneda, and pay more attention to the landing time.

japan.q: How many temples before they stop working?
japan.call: Two major temples a day, three if they are spread, and never four.

turkey.q: Should the internal flights sit on the same ticket as the flight home?
turkey.call: Put the internal legs on the international ticket where the route allows it, and treat a separate-ticket internal leg as one you have insured yourself.

turkey.q: What are you exposed to, and what does a policy answer?
turkey.call: Establish two things before departure and the work is done: whether your policy is primary or secondary, and whether the activities you have already booked appear in its exclusions.

turkey.q: Which of the four licence thresholds is the one that binds you?
turkey.call: Carry the permit even though Turkish law does not require it, and read the rental contract rather than an article about rental contracts.

turkey.q: What can actually leave the country with you?
turkey.call: Buy new things freely, and treat any object presented as old as a decision rather than a purchase.

turkey.q: How much does it cost to hold Turkish lira?
turkey.call: Establish your own issuer's structure before you leave, then choose the machine rather than the amount.

turkey.q: Which channel carries the thing that unfreezes your card?
turkey.call: Keep the home number reachable for the whole trip on the cheapest voice-and-text arrangement your carrier sells, and treat the eSIM as data only — then read your issuer's card settings before you fly rather than from Turkey.

turkey.q: When is the ground move the safe one rather than the slow one?
turkey.call: Put the overland leg where the itinerary is tightest — immediately before the international return — and fly the legs with slack behind them.

rome.call: Sleep inside the core; treat a metro address as a downgrade, not a discount.

rome.q: Do you need transit tickets at all?
rome.call: If you slept in the core, skip the pass and tap a contactless card.

rome.q: Train, or the fixed-fare taxi from the airport?
rome.call: Central base, first night, real luggage: take the fixed-fare taxi and don’t feel fleeced.

rome.q: How do you fit the ancient core into a day?
rome.call: Give the ancient core its own half-day, and start with the Forum at opening.

rome.q: What does “skip the line” actually skip at the Vatican?
rome.call: Book the official timed ticket for the Museums; for St Peter’s, buy nothing and go early.

rome.q: What must you book in advance — and how far?
rome.call: Book the three that sell out the moment your dates are firm; leave the rest to the trip week.

rome.q: Cards or cash — and the one prompt that quietly overcharges you?
rome.call: Choose euros at every machine, tip like a local, and carry a little cash.

rome.q: How do you avoid eating badly in a city this good at food?
rome.call: Don’t collect restaurant names; walk ninety seconds off the sight.

rome.q: If you have a fourth day, where does it go?
rome.call: For a single spare day, take Ostia Antica; save Pompeii for a trip that can spare a whole day to it.
